page: Vultr voc-g-24c-96gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance engineered for balanced, multi-threaded workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical AMD EPYC cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. The processor features 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and standard instruction extensions including AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory totals 96 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provisioned via a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without integrated GPU hardware.

Performance metrics indicate competent processing and data handling across varied execution profiles. The server scored 3,208.88 in single-core stress-ng tests, ranking in the top tier, while multi-core stress-ng reached 74,749.71. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 1,746.0 and a multi-core score of 14,468.0, with solid results in image processing (14,143.0) and Clang software compilation (28,050.0). Synthetic benchmarks demonstrated strong memory subsystem results with a PassMark memory score of 2,891.74 alongside uncached read bandwidth of 126.87 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 61.71 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the configuration handled 39.86 million Redis SET operations per second and sustained static web delivery throughput of 21.63 GB/sec.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides balanced resource distribution, avoiding the cost overhead of disproportionately large memory allocations while delivering dedicated AMD EPYC compute density. A notable architectural limitation is the absence of AVX-512, which limits throughput on specialized matrix mathematics and dense vector extensions. However, for standard server workloads, the combination of dedicated execution threads, solid NVMe performance, and consistent memory bandwidth offers predictable throughput. The server is well aligned for mid-tier relational database hosting, continuous integration build servers, multi-threaded backend services, and general-purpose enterprise application hosting.
description: Vultr voc-g-24c-96gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz, paired with 96 GB of system RAM to establish a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Local persistent storage is handled by a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes a dedicated public IPv4 address with zero GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier stress-ng single-core output of 3,208.88 and strong multi-core throughput of 74,749.71, complemented by a PassMark memory rating of 2,891.74 and Redis throughput reaching 39.86 million operations per second. While lacking AVX-512 support, the hardware profile offers balanced resource distribution and high concurrency. The instance is suited for multi-threaded application servers, relational database instances, CI/CD pipeline workers, and web serving infrastructures.
